data.purpose: Approve a four-week pilot to improve governance transparency, verify proposal and voting records against CyberChain, and evaluate evidence-based AI assistance.
data.description: Run a four-week CyberGovAI pilot covering an independent governance security review, a proposal and voting transparency dashboard, and an AI assistant that answers questions using verified proposal documents and read-only blockchain data. The proposed budget is EUR 12,000: EUR 6,000 for security review, EUR 3,000 for dashboard improvements, EUR 2,000 for AI evaluation, and EUR 1,000 contingency. Deliverables include a security findings report, an updated governance dashboard, a reproducible AI evaluation dataset, and a final pilot report. This is demonstration data; approval does not automatically transfer funds or execute contract changes.

No supplier has been appointed and no payment recipient is specified.
4. Delivery schedule
Day 1 means the pilot kickoff after approval and confirmation of an implementation owner. These delivery
milestones are separate from the on-chain voting start and end times.
Deadline

Day 7
Inventory and review plan

Publish measured results, limitations and

5. Success criteria
Every factual AI answer must cite the supporting document excerpt or structured governance evidence.
Unsupported questions must be answered without fabricated facts. On-chain checks must record the actual
chain ID, contract address and pinned block number. Multi-question requests must preserve question order
and show separate results. Conversation history must reopen without requiring a second wallet connection
when the wallet is already connected.
Evaluation should report routing, citation checks, tool outcomes, latency and model-reported token usage.
Missing measurements must remain unknown. No numerical accuracy threshold or claim of achieved
performance is established by this proposal.

RISKS, CONTROLS AND VERIFICATION
6. Risks and mitigations
Risk
Planned mitigation

answers

snapshot

blockchain
Display both values, provenance and the specific discrepancy;
do not silently overwrite records.
Private credentials reaching the
browser
Keep operator tokens and database credentials server-side;
reuse authenticated backend authorization.
PDF text unavailable to retrieval
Check document linkage, SHA-256 verification and a compatible
text/embedding index.
Budget or delivery overrun
Review milestones weekly and require explicit approval for
scope changes.
7. Governance and voting
The proposed voting options are Approve, Reject and Abstain. Actual eligibility, assigned members, vote
totals, quorum and final result are governed by the deployed contract and live application state. This PDF
does not establish a quorum percentage or claim an outcome.
For the demonstration, configure voting dates and assign test-wallet addresses in the UI. Assignment counts
and votes must be queried from the application or chain after creation. The document intentionally contains
no invented proposal ID, contract address, transaction hash, block number or current vote tally.
8. Evidence boundaries
This PDF supports questions about the proposed purpose, scope, budget, schedule, deliverables, risks and
success criteria. It does not prove that a security audit has been completed, that funds were released, that a
supplier was selected or that any proposal was approved. It does not identify a secret password or API
credentials.
Document linkage and hash verification establish which bytes were attached to the proposal. They do not
establish that the proposal claims are true or that the described work has happened. Live governance facts
require independent database or blockchain reads.

Proposal title
CyberGovAI Governance Security and Transparency Pilot
Decision requested
Approve the proposed pilot and its EUR 12,000 budget.
1. Purpose and agenda
Approve a four-week pilot to improve governance transparency, verify proposal and voting records against
CyberChain, and evaluate evidence-based AI assistance.
The agenda has three parts: independently review governance security, improve visibility of proposal and
voting records, and assess whether AI answers are supported by the linked proposal PDF and actual
blockchain reads.
2. Proposed scope
The security review covers proposal creation, member assignment, vote recording, result finalization, wallet
authentication and access control. The transparency dashboard presents proposal status, recorded votes,
transaction references and database-to-chain discrepancies. The AI assistant summarizes linked documents,
cites supporting excerpts and separates unavailable facts from observed facts.
Demonstration status
This document is synthetic test data. It is not a real auditor quotation, an approved budget or evidence of
completed work. Approval does not automatically transfer funds or execute contract changes. A separate
authorized process is required for any payment or implementation.

4. Success criteria
Deliver two workshops and a final participation guide. Record actual attendance against the planned target of
30 participants. Include at least five worked examples covering proposal interpretation, PDF citations, wallet
safety, vote confirmation and database-to-chain comparison. Report feedback without claiming a
predetermined improvement score.
5. Risks and mitigations
Risk
Planned mitigation
Low attendance
Share invitations early and offer a recorded walkthrough.
Wallet or transaction confusion
Use test wallets and guided examples; never request private keys
or recovery phrases.
Misunderstanding AI answers
Show source excerpts and explain that citations require inspection.
RPC or network interruption
Use saved examples clearly labeled with their observation time.
Personal information in feedback
Collect only necessary information and publish aggregated
findings.
6. Governance and evidence boundaries
Voting options are Approve, Reject and Abstain. Actual member assignments, voting dates, vote totals and
final outcome must come from the application and contract after proposal creation. This PDF does not specify
a quorum percentage, an on-chain proposal ID, a contract address or transaction hashes.
This is synthetic data for a live software demonstration. The document describes proposed activities and
targets; it does not prove that workshops occurred, 30 people attended or the budget was approved. Approval
does not automatically release funds or execute contract changes. No password or API credentials are
provided.

Community Governance Training
and Participation Pilot
A three-week initiative to help members understand proposals, inspect evidence and participate
safely in DAO voting.
Reference
CG-DEMO-2026-02 / version 1.0

cyber-demo-dao
Proposal title
Community Governance Training and Participation Pilot
Type / duration
STANDARD / 21 days after kickoff
Decision requested
Approve the proposed EUR 4,500 training pilot.
1. Purpose and proposed activities
Improve members' understanding of DAO proposals, evidence and wallet-based voting through two guided
workshops and an accessible participation guide. The planned attendance target is 30 participants across the
pilot; this is a target, not a recorded member or voter count.
Workshop 1 covers proposal purpose, supporting PDFs, source citations and differences between proposed
commitments and completed work. Workshop 2 covers connected-wallet use, voting eligibility, transaction
confirmation and comparison of database records with blockchain observations.

PROJECT PROPOSAL
TITLE
Community Clean-Up Initiative
PURPOSE
To create a cleaner, healthier, and more welcoming neighborhood by encouraging
community participation in a local clean-up activity.
DESCRIPTION
This project will bring together local volunteers for a one-day clean-up of shared public
spaces. Participants will collect litter, sort recyclable materials, and help improve the
appearance of the area. The initiative will also promote environmental awareness and
teamwork.
